Share:Print page Facebook share Linkedin share X social media share Start-Up Challenge Start-Up Challenge 2027 NIA Start-Up Challenge and Accelerator: Driving Aging Innovation NIA is excited to announce the 2027 NIA Start-Up Challenge and Accelerator. Through this Challenge, NIA is seeking early-stage entrepreneurs with innovative ideas for technologies to improve healthy aging. Submissions will be accepted from December 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027 . Visit www.nih.gov/challenges/2027-nia-start-challenge-accelerator to learn more and submit. Register now(link is external)") for the informational webinar on December 3, 2026. In addition to their innovative idea, submitters must demonstrate a need for the significant resources provided by the accelerator program, including: - Cash prizes of $24,000 for up to 21 finalist teams - Additional cash prizes of $70,000 for 7 winning teams - Entrepreneurial training sessions led by industry experts - 1:1 mentorship from experienced founders and investors - In-depth pitch coaching - Virtual and in-person networking with key industry partners - Introduction to the NIA and NIH Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) funding programs Important Dates - Challenge Launched: Sept. 1, 2026 - Registration and Submission Start/End Dates: December 1, 2026 – January 15, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET - Informational Webinar: December 3, 2026, 1PM ET - Register Now!(link is external)") - Stage 1 Finalists Announced: May 2027 - Stage 1 Accelerator Program: June – November 2027 - Final Submission and Pitch Due: November 2027 - Stage 2 Winners Announced: January 2028 About Submissions This Challenge invites submissions from researchers and innovators who are new to entrepreneurship or actively seeking to pursue it, and who propose innovative, science-driven technologies with the potential to improve the health and well-being of older adults. Strong submissions must clearly describe how the participating individual or team would substantially benefit from intensive entrepreneurial training, mentorship, and the cash prizes provided by the Challenge. Submissions must also describe how the proposed solution will be substantially differentiated from existing commercialized products, and how it would expand the types of technologies and approaches already supported by the NIA SBIR and STTR programs. Existing technologies funded by the NIA SBIR and STTR programs can be found through the NIH Reporter database. This Challenge is interested in ideas for innovative t … evant factors, including biological, social, behavioral, economic, environmental, and regional factors, that impact a solution’s utility. How to Enter Registration and Submission Process The submission link will open on December 1, 2026 at www.nih.gov/challenges/2027-nia-start-challenge-accelerator. Plan to register and provide a submission by the deadline of 11:59 PM ET on January 15, 2027. Do not include any confidential or proprietary information in your submission materials. By submitting materials in response to this Challenge, you agree to allow the National Institute on Aging to publish all or parts of your submission materials on www.nia.nih.gov. For Teams: Each participating Team is required to identify a Team Lead who will register and submit on behalf of the Team members. The Team Lead manages all communication with the Challenge sponsors and, if a cash prize is won, will receive the full amount of the prize . To be eligible to receive a cash prize, the Team Lead must be a citizen or permanent resident of the United States. If a dispute over the Team Lead's identity cannot be satisfactorily resolved by NIH, the submission will be considered ineligible. For Entities: Each participating Entity is required to identify a Point of Contact who will register and submit on behalf of the Entity. The Point of Contact is responsible for all communications with the Challenge sponsors. In the event of winning a cash prize, the prize will be paid directly to the Entity, not to the Point of Contact. To be eligible to receive a cash prize, the Entity must be incorporated in and maintain a primary place of business in the United States. As stated in the Participation Rules, submitters intending to use Federal grant or cooperative agreement funds to develop their Challenge submissions or to fund efforts in support of their Challenge submissions must register for and participate in the Challenge as an Entity on behalf of the awardee institution or organization. If a Point of Contact’s identity dispute cannot be resolved to NIH’s satisfaction, the submission will be considered ineligible. Submission Requirements Multiple submissions are allowed, however, only one submission from each individual, team, or entity will be selected for participation as a Finalist. Late submissions will not be accepted. Explore the Start-Up Challenge - About the Challenge and Accelerator - Eligibility and Rules - Judging Criteria and Prizes - Past Start-Up Challenge Cohorts - More Information Statutory Authority to Conduct the Challenge The National Institute on Aging is conducting the NIA Start-Up Challenge under the America Creating Opportunities to Meaningfully Promote Excellence in Technology, Education, and Science (COMPETES) Reauthorization Act of 2010, as amended [15 U.S.C. § 3719 ]. This Challenge supports the Institute’s statutory authority by advancing early-stage research and facilitating the translation of scientific discoveries into evidence-based technologies that improve the health and well-being of older adults. It also strengthens the biomedical research workforce by training and empowering emerging innovators and entrepreneurs to address the needs of older Americans. Together, these objectives directly advance the NIA’s mission. Last updated: September 1, 2026 nia.nih.gov An official website

The Hollomon Health Innovation Challenge (HIC) is an annual student competition that encourages innovative solutions to major health-related problems facing the world today. Held each winter, the HIC brings together student teams from different schools and disciplines to identify a health or health care problem, design a product, process, or service to address it, and create a business summary that demonstrates market interest and the potential for their idea. What is Your Idea? Students can compete with any product, process, or service that highlights a new approach to wellness, care and treatment, safety, or access. This includes medical devices, therapeutics, digital health interventions, healthcare workflow solutions, ideas that address mental or community health, and more. In recent years, new enabling technologies have contributed to rapid growth in health innovation. This is an area where your creativity and passion can thrive! Want to Learn More? Find information below about the HIC timeline, eligibility, entry requirements, and resources to help you prepare your application. View the recording from our Virtual Information Session for the 2023 HIC. Dates & Deadlines The application site opens for submissions on Tuesday, December 1, 2026 and applications are due by 12:00 noon on Monday, January 25, 2027 . The competition begins with the initial online Screening Round between February 4 and February 11. NOTE: TEAM MEMBER PROFILES MUST BE COMPLETED BEFORE THE APPLICATION CAN BE SUBMITTED! We recommend notifying your team members of this requirement and encouraging them to submit their profile well before the deadline. Applications may be accessed and edited up until the deadline. The competition begins with an online Screening Round open to judges only between January 27 and February 3. After, 21 teams are selected and invited to compete in the live Final Round held on Thursday, February 25, 2027 View the schedule below for information sessions and workshops designed to help student teams prepare for the 2027 Health Innovation Challenge. 2027 Competition Rounds & Deliverables --- --- Event Date Applications Open Monday, December 1, 2026 Information Sessions Thursday, January 14 – Virtual<br Thursday, January 21 – In-person Applications Close <br Deliverable: 5/7-page Business Summary<br (see REQUIREMENTS & CRITERIA below) Monday, January 25 – Noon Screening Round (Judges Only) January 27 – February 3 Announcement of 21 advancing teams Thursday, February 4 – 2 PM by email Final Round Resource Night Mandatory for all advancing teams Wednesday, February 18– Virtual Final Round Pitch Workshop Mandatory for all advancing teams Tuesday, February 24 – Virtual Final Round Access <br Deliverable: 1-page Business Summary<br (see REQUIREMENTS & CRITERIA below) Thursday, February 18 – Noon Challenge Day <br Deliverable: 60-second pitch presented on stage<br + tradeshow-style event Thursday, February 25 – Morning/Afternoon Reception and Awards Ceremony Networking & Winners Announcement Thursday, February 25 – Evening Entry Requirements Any student in good standing from a Cascadia Corridor (Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and British Columbia) and Alaska college or university who is enrolled in a degree-seeking program can participate in the Hollomon Health Innovation Challenge (HIC). Teams must be student-led. Non-students can be members of a team, generally as advisers, but they can’t present at the HIC, nor can they receive prize money. The most successful teams have members with various skill sets from various departments, including built environments, law, engineering, business, policy, etc. Therefore, cross-disciplinary teams are highly encouraged. pages.text: skip to main content Share on social media share facebook;) share twitter;) share linkedin;) Tags Children and Youth Innovation topics Announcements Calling All Innovators: Telosity Mental Health Innovation Challenge Now Open for Applications Calling All Innovators: Telosity Mental Health Innovation Challenge Now Open for Applications Detail page We are excited to announce that the Meadows Institute has joined venture capital fund, Telosity Ventures, to launch a Mental Health Innovation Challenge. The challenge is designed to catalyze and accelerate innovation by helping digital startups and non-profits access capital, develop, and launch their bold ideas. The challenge is targeted towards innovators creating solutions that positively impact the industry and accelerate transformative solutions to better serve people with mental health challenges. Innovation Challenge themes include pediatric mental health, suicide prevention, neurodevelopmental challenges, and more. Innovators are encouraged to apply for a chance to pitch their ideas to healthcare leaders and investors and potentially earn cash prizes, as well as opportunities for mentorship and further investment. Meadows Institute experts will participate in coaching challenge winners on effectively implementing and measuring the outcomes of their transformative solutions. Through our partnership, led by the Meadows Institute’s Innovation Team, we welcome the venture capital community’s interest in addressing our nation’s mental health crisis and invite innovators to apply. We look forward to this partnership creating opportunities for leading-edge solutions in the Texas marketplace and beyond. Apply by April 5, 2023 The application period is open now through April 5. Finalists will be selected in late April and participate in a demo day in May. Learn more and apply. Telosity Ventures is a venture capital firm that invests in pre-seed and seed-stage startups focused on digital wellness and mental health. They work to connect industry experts, partners, entrepreneurs, and investors to actively support the growth of their portfolio companies. Companies include MindRight Health, Neolth, Manatee, Ksana, and more. What can the Meadows Institute do for you? Get in touch to learn more about our services and how we can help your community. The Brain Innovation Days Pitch Competition is an opportunity for you to pitch your business to join the running for the Jury and/or Public Prize. Our annual Pitch Competition aims to provide start-ups the opportunity to showcase great examples of brain innovation in Europe that can create positive impact — innovations and solutions that will improve the quality of life of people with brain disorders (neurological and mental) and support clinicians, researchers, caregivers, industry, and society as a whole. Being selected as a finalist for the Pitch Competition grants you a waived ticket to the Brain Innovation Days event taking place in Brussels (Belgium) on 18-19 November 2026. This year’s edition will feature a Pecha Kucha-style format, bringing a dynamic and engaging twist to the pitch competition. Pitch your business to join the running for expert & investor mentorship, prominent event exposure, in-depth jury feedback, networking opportunities, an exclusive video interview, and your own Brain Talks podcast episode and much more! Please note that applications are open until 30 June 2026 . Finalists will be announced in July. Note that your start-up has to be 7 years or younger and can submit only one pitch. The Pitch Competition applications have closed now. However, startups can still showcase their innovations at the event. Apply for a spot in the Innovation Hall! Note: Due to a large number of applications, the results will be announced in August. 19 November 2026 Take part in the 2026 Brain Innovation Days Pitch Competition! The Pitch Competition will take place on Thursday, 19 November 2026 in Brussels (Belgium) at Area 42. pages.text: 4 Cohorts Launched Since 2023 51 Companies In Our Portfolio Pre-Seed, Seed, Series A Company Stages $1.45 Billion Cumulative Funds Raised by Portfolio 1.5 Million People Served by Portfolio Companies Shaping a Hopeful Future for Mental Health through Innovation & Entrepreneurship The One Mind Accelerator backs bold and determined founders of early-stage startups with the network, education and capital to build category-defining companies that radically improve the lives of people facing mental health challenges. Launched in 2023, the highly competitive program selects a cohort of 10-15 startups each year from hundreds of applicants. The companies span care model innovations to diagnostics and treatments, and are prioritized for serious mental illness, youth mental health, maternal mental health, and precision psychiatry. Designed from the ground up with a specific focus on mental health, the selected founders participate in ten weeks of programming, with in-person opening and closing weeks in Menlo Park, CA. The program leverages One Mind’s vast and influential network of leaders and domain experts to help the startups take their innovations to market faster and with greater impact for people facing mental illness. Supported by leading philanthropists and corporations, the One Mind Accelerator seeks to usher in a new era of value-based, affordable, accessible, equitable and personalized mental healthcare. pages.text: Headstream's News Headstream Announces the 2026 Members of its Residency and Accelerator Programs Founders will sharpen their business models, learn from industry experts, and connect with peers around the same goal: helping more young people thrive NEW YORK, NY - Headstream, a SecondMuse initiative aimed at enhancing the mental well-being of adolescents in marginalized communities, today announced the members of its 2026 Residency and Accelerator cohorts, a program supported by Pivotal Ventures. Over the next 16 weeks, these founders will build, grow, and shape what’s next for youth mental well-being. The Headstream program provides a unique opportunity to work with youth co-creators on messaging, user experience, and retention. This year’s Residency founder group welcomes six companies: - Shelby Robbins of Antelope Recovery, providing virtual OP & IOP services to justice-involved youth across the entire justice continuum, specializing in criminogenic needs. - Michelle Turner of Here Now Health, the first virtual healthcare company purpose built for children and young adults impacted by the child welfare system. - Julia Belt of Navi, helping teens create action plans to navigate challenges through self-guided mini activities, backed by 10 years of clinical research. - Gregory Milnarik of Koomba, an athlete development infrastructure for youth and college sports, connecting athletes to credentialed coaches in mental performance and sport nutrition. - Jasmine Schembri-Stothar  … background. Four of this year’s Residency companies are graduates of the 2025 Accelerator program. Fifteen companies will participate in the 2026 Accelerator program. Two thirds of this year’s startups are founded by individuals who identify as women and 87% who identify as BIPOC+. The Accelerator provides participants with $30,000 in non-dilutive funding, virtual programming led by industry experts, a network of fellow founders and supporters, coaching tailored to individual well-being, a curriculum shaped around the cohort’s needs, collaboration opportunities with the Youth Co-Creator Club, and a fully funded in-person gathering to kick off the program. Members of the 2026 cohort include: - Asher Herbstman of Clear30, the first evidence-based platform addressing the growing cannabis crisis. Clear30 delivers education, intervention, and assessment to the millions struggling with no support. - Mahmoud Khedr of Healers Health, AI-powered social care navigation that matches and enrolls teens and families to the jobs, benefits, mental health resources, and community programs that help them thrive. - Olivia DeRamus of Co … oped, and implemented innovative programs and financial solutions that unlock new opportunities, expand access to capital, and drive economic transformation. Our work spans 190+ countries and territories. Learn more at secondmuse.com Media Contact Molly Galler, Public Relations molly.galler@secondmuse.com Similar Posts Headstream's News Headstream Announces the 2026 Members of its Residency and Accelerator Programs Founders will sharpen their business models, learn from industry experts, and connect with peers around the same goal: helping more young people thrive .png) Headstream's News Why Headstream Programs Matter for the Future of Youth Mental Well-Being Youth mental health systems are struggling, even as more young people turn to digital tools for support. Headstream meets this momen … d Youth Co-Creator Club, founders refine and scale products while young people shape the tools designed for them. The result is stronger, more relevant mental health technology and a growing ecosystem built to better support youth well-being. Headstream's News Meeting the Moment: How the K‑12 Mental Health Tech Navigator Is Helping Schools Support Student Well‑Being Schools are at the frontlines of student mental health and well-being, but rising needs and limited resources make support challenging. The K-12 Mental Health Tech Navigator, created by Headstream with The Jed Foundation and Meadows Mental Health Policy Institute, helps districts identify and fund digital tools that supplement care when counselors and staff are stretched thin. Learn how the updated Navigator offers interactive guidance, expanded resources, and actionable pathways to ensure every student has access to the support they deserve.

pages.text: 0 Immerse your mental health startup in real world expertise Prepare for the opportunity to partner with a dedicated Mental Health Fund and a leading Mental Healthcare Provider. TRANSFORMING MENTAL HEALTH Find out more EXPRESS INTEREST View fullsize Why have we launched the Immersion Programme? Millions of people globally face unmet mental health needs, with limited evidence-based solutions addressing clinical disorders. Mental health systems urgently require innovative, scalable technologies to improve prediction, therapy, management and system efficiency. The gap between consumer wellbeing tools and clinical-grade solutions highlights a CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY for impactful tech innovation. 01 Unmet needs 02 Clinical focus 03 System efficiency 04 Evidence-based solutions ABOUT THE PROGRAMME This free, highly selective 12-WEEK PROGRAMME SUPPORTS STARTUPS tackling depression, anxiety, and psychosis with expert mentorship, sector-specific guidance, and investment opportunities. Companies ready for the next stage will be considered for investment by the Innovations in Mental Health Fund, this would enable them to gain access to generate real-world evidence with UK NHS partners and accelerate growth through continued support. The programme is open to companies operating anywhere in the world and we are welcoming of global applicants. We received applications from companies in 18 countries for the first programme and half of the participating Founders came from outside the UK. •⁠ ⁠Access to top sector, clinical, and investment expertise •⁠ ⁠One-on-one mentorship tailored to your startup's needs •⁠ ⁠Focus on founder wellbeing and company-building best practices TAILORED SUPPORT •⁠ ⁠Support navigating healthcare markets and regulatory challenges •⁠ ⁠Real-world evidence generation opportunit … d healthcare advisors PREP FOR INVESTMENT Our Team & Partners Dr. Pooja Sikka General Partner Daniel Dickens Managing Partner Aahuti Rai Executive Lead, Immersion Programme Jing Wei Luo Head of Legal and Operations Dr. Aditi Babel Associate Ready to find out more? Read our FAQ for more details and follow us on LinkedIn to be the first to know when applications reopen. READ OUR FAQ WHO SHOULD APPLY We seek startups with innovative digital solutions targeting mental illness, ready for real-world testing and market entry. 01 At minimum, you should have a product prototype ready for real-world testing based on sound assumptions, a clear evidence base and data (where applicable). 02 You must have a focus on depression, anxiety and psychosis-related disorders. 03 Your company could be pre-revenue, pre-seed or pre-GTM, including spin-outs and new company formations. However, we are also keen to meet companies at seed and seed+ stage and support will be tailored around your key milestones at this stage of development. 04 Your company can be based anywhere in the world, however you must have an intention to operate in the UK within 18 months of participating in the programme. This could be initial validation work, ongoing R&D and/or bringing products to market. 05 The IMH Programme is focused specifically on digital mental health solutions, prioritising those innovations with a software component. However, we will consider hardware, medtech and techbio innovations focused on mental illness. Particular interest is given to AI-enabled solutions, provided the AI application is purposeful. 06 You should have a good understanding of the market opportunity aligning to one of six categories of products related to delivering an impactful technology: 1 . Better and more equitable access to care 2 . Improving clinical/health outcomes 3 . Earlier diagnosis and intervention or prevention of relapse 4 . Monitoring treatment or supporting precision treatment 5 . Changing health behaviour, including self-management and awareness, monitoring progress or treatment 6 . Improving cost-effectiveness of access, diagnosis, or management. 07 Companies which focus on wellbeing and are not aligned with clinical conditions are not eligible to apply. Key dates for Programme Two Friday, October 10th Deadline for submission, 6pm GMT Thursday, October 16th Interviews for international applicants Friday, October 17th Interviews for UK-based applicants Monday, October 20th Successful applicants to first immersion programme notified. Tuesday, November 25th – Thursday November 27th Immersion programme starts in London (participants expected to be in London for these 3 days) December 2025 – February 2026 Portfolio decisions: TBD Immersion Programme continues remotely: TBD APPLY NOW Expression of interest Applications for the next Innovations in Mental He… Applications for the next Innovations in Mental Health programme are currently closed. Please share your details and we'll be in touch to let you know when recruitment for the next programme begins. 1 Please tell us your name FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS - What is Innovations in Mental Health? Europe's first mental health-focused venture investor partnered with a public health system that invests in transformative technologies. Its Immersion Programme supports innovators addressing depression, anxiety, and psychosis with mentorship, NHS partnership and investment opportunities, focusing on overcoming health tech barriers and accelerating growth. - What is the Fund's ticket size? Ticket sizes range from £250k–£1m, averaging £500k, with flexibility based on innovation stage. The Fund leads and co-invests in early-stage ventures, prioritising impactful, scalable mental health technologies. - What type of ventures are you looking for? The fund invests in ventures addressing unmet needs in depression, anxiety, and psychosis. Ventures should align with clinical outcomes, be globally diverse, and demonstrate potential for UK scale-up to enhance the mental health system. Digital-first solutions with global scalability are highly prioritised. - What type of ventures are not suitable for the programme? Companies focused on wellbeing and not aligned with clinical conditions are not eligible for funding or programme participation. - What kind of funding is provided? The programme itself does not provide funding. Post-programme, select companies may receive bespoke investment offers from the IMH Fund. - How much does the Immersion Programme cost, and does Meridian Health Ventures take equity? Participation is free, and Meridian Health Ventures takes no equity. Post-programme, select companies may receive bespoke investment offers from the IMH Fund. Each participating company must cover their own costs to attend the 3-day in person part of the programme in London. Companies from LMICs or underrepresented groups from outside the UK may be considered for a small travel budget based on means. - How does the partnership with the NHS Trust work? Portfolio companies will have the opportunity to allocate investment capital towards tailored support from South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust (SLaM), including mentorship, clinical studies, real-world evidence generation, patient engagement, data access, grant support, implementation guidance, and NHS system navigation. - Where is the programme based? Do I have to relocate? The first week of the programme is in London and requires in-person attendance. Participants are responsible for covering their own travel and accommodation expenses. Companies from LMICs or underrepresented groups from outside the UK may be considered for a small travel budget based on means. Subsequent sessions are remote. - How can I find out more about the Immersion Programme before I apply? Please browse this website and FAQs for information about the Immersion Programme. When we reopen for new applications we will organise information webinars to provide you with further information. You may also contact us at hello@innovationsinmentalhealth.com with specific queries. ​ - How many ventures will be in each programme? Up to 15 ventures will be accepted into the programme for this cohort. - When will I learn if my application has been successful? For any applications already submitted you will be notified as per the timetable communicated at the time of your application. We are currently not open for any new applications. - What does the interview process look like? Interviews, conducted by Meridian Health Ventures team members, and possibly external stakeholders, will assess alignment with the programme's objectives and the potential for success. - Will I receive any feedback if I'm not successful? Applicants invited to interview will receive feedback. Due to high application volume, feedback cannot be provided to all applicants. Partner content April 23, 2025·2 min read Lisa Palchynska Editor-in-Chief, Vestbee Insights Last call for startups improving well-being to apply for NN Social Innovation Startup Award to win €100,000 The NN Social Innovation Startup Award, powered by Rubio, is back after a successful debut in 2024. Designed to support early-stage startups using technology to improve mental, physical, or financial well-being, the award returns to spotlight innovation with purpose at The Next Web Conference on June 19 in Amsterdam. About the NN Social Innovation Startup Award The award is a joint initiative by NN Group, an international financial services company, and Rubio Impact Ventures, a leading Dutch impact investment fund. It aims to empower a new generation of mission-driven founders creating scalable solutions that address Europe’s growing well-being gap. Selected startups will pitch on stage at The Next Web Conference, one of Europe’s most influential tech events. The winner will receive a €100,000 grant from a total €200,000 fund, and access to a one-year venture development program. This includes tailored mentoring, investor readiness support, and connections to a mission-aligned network of partners and backers. “Some of the most impactful startups are built by people with deep personal insight into the problems they’re solving. But turning that into a scalable business, especially in sectors like mental health, healthcare access, or financial resilience, is incredibly hard without the right kind of support. This award was created to fill that gap. Not just with funding, but with true partnership. What we’re building is more than a pitch event — it’s a community of innovators and allies committed to changing the system, so that tech-driven solutions for well-being become the norm, not the exception,” Ilonka Jankovich, Venture Partner at Rubio Impact Ventures, comments. Why is it important In Europe, well-being is under pressure. Rising health disparities, increasing mental health needs, and uneven financ … lived experience and deep insight into these issues gain the resources and connections needed to scale. Last year’s winner, The Linghos — a Polish AI-powered platform improving pediatric speech therapy — has since expanded its reach with support from NN and Rubio. Runner-ups Whispp and Bugeto also joined the venture development program. Who should apply The call is open to early-stage tech startups across Europe building scalable and inclusive solutions to improve mental, physical, or financial well-being. If your startup is driven by impact and ready to grow, this opportunity is for you. How to apply Applications are open until April 30, 2025 . Startups can apply via the official website: https://www.socialinnovationaward.com. Notify meNotify me when it reopens About this competition The Wellcome Prize for Mental Health Science, in partnership with Nature, champions novel and impactful interventions designed to transform the lives of individuals grappling with anxiety, depression, and psychosis. This prestigious international prize seeks to accelerate the development, adoption, and policy prioritization of effective solutions, fostering a global ecosystem of innovation in mental health. Organized by Wellcome, a global charitable foundation dedicated to solving urgent health challenges, and Nature, a world-leading science publisher known for advancing discovery, the prize leverages significant resources and platforms. Wellcome supports cutting-edge research across life, health, and wellbeing, with a strong focus on mental health, infectious disease, and climate and health. Nature, through its Nature Awards initiatives, extends its mission to support outstanding researchers and drive real-world change beyond traditional publication. The prize aims to not only provide substantial financial backing but also to elevate mental health science globally. By celebrating breakthrough research and generating enthusiasm among policymakers, funders, and the public, the initiative strives to encourage greater investment and collaboration in this critical field. This multi-stage competition identifies and rewards teams whose interventions demonstrate exceptional promise in creating transformative change for people affected by severe mental health conditions. Beyond monetary support, successful teams will gain unparalleled global visibility through Wellcome and Nature's extensive platforms, crucial connections with policymakers and funders, and practical support to navigate the complexities of accelerating adoption and integrating their interventions into policy frameworks. This comprehensive package is designed to propel innovative mental health solutions from research into real-world impact. Following the application submission, entries undergo a rigorous screening and evaluation by an expert committee comprising leading scientists, clinicians, policymakers, and innovators. Shortlisted teams are identified based on the novelty, scientific rigor, potential impact, and feasibility of their proposed mental health interventions. These teams may be required to provide further information or participate in in-depth interviews. Finalists are then selected and announced, leading to a comprehensive review by a Grand Jury, which ultimately determines the single prize winner. The entire process, from application opening to winner announcement, spans approximately 13 months, ensuring a thorough and fair assessment of all submissions. Program contact Sponsored Frequently Asked Questions What is the primary goal of the Wellcome Prize for Mental Health Science? The prize aims to accelerate the development, adoption, and policy prioritization of effective interventions for anxiety, depression, and psychosis. It also seeks to generate enthusiasm for mental health science among policymakers, funders, and the public to encourage greater investment in research. Who is eligible to apply for this prize? The prize is open to research teams worldwide developing new, effective interventions for anxiety, depression, or psychosis. Eligible teams can be based at universities, research institutes, hospitals, government or not-for-profit organizations, or small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), including startups and companies. What are the prize amounts? One winning team will receive US$1 million (approximately ₹9.52 crore). Additionally, three finalists (runners-up) will each be awarded US$250,000 (approximately ₹2.38 crore). Is there a geographical restriction for applicants? No, applications are welcome from around the world. The program is explicitly international with no country restrictions. What kind of support is offered beyond the financial prize? Beyond financial backing, the prize provides significant global visibility through Wellcome and Nature's platforms, strategic connections with key stakeholders, and practical support to help winning interventions progress towards widespread adoption and successful policy integration. This includes elements like mentorship, investor access, and market entry support. What is the application deadline? The authoritative application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 5:30 AM IST, as indicated on the Submittable application portal. For more information on upgrading please see browser-update.org. 14 May 20266-minute read - Mental health Share this page - Share with Email - Share with LinkedIn - Share with Bluesky - Share with X - Share with Facebook 14 May 20266-minute read - The prize, in partnership with Nature , will celebrate breakthroughs in mental health science. It aims to accelerate translation, influence policy and transform lives - This award champions new pharmacological, psychological, social and digital interventions from around the world - The overall winner will receive USD 1 million, and three finalists will be awarded USD 250,000 each. Professor Miranda Wolpert, Director of Mental Health at Wellcome said: "We are in the midst of a revolution in mental health science, with groundbreaking advances in research already leading to new ways of understanding and treating mental health problems. The Prize will celebrate the amazing new discoveries that are set to transform people’s lives." By highlighting interventions that demonstrate meaningful improvements in outcomes, the prize will showcase the opportunities and progress within mental health. Mental health science has the power to transform lives, and breakthroughs are already changing how conditions are understood and treated. Many conditions are increasingly manageable, particularly with earlier and more effective interventions, offering new hope for many people. There has been cutting-edge research that has been leading to breakthroughs in recent years, a seismic shift in mental health science that the Prize seeks to celebrate. The scale of the challenge remains significant. More than a billion people live with mental health conditions worldwide, yet many are held back as systems are struggling to respond.1The global median percentage of government health spending on mental health is just 2.1%. Spending is as low as USD 0.04 per person in low-income countries compared to USD 65.89 in high-income settings.1,2 The global median number of speciali … hysical illness such as cardiovascular disease, reduced quality of life and premature mortality.3 They also drive productivity and economic losses that far outweigh healthcare costs, with an estimated 12 billion productive work days lost each year globally to anxiety and depression.3 Dr Magdalena Skipper, Editor-in-Chief of Nature and Chair of the Prize’s judging panel said: "Prevention and treatment of key medical issues such as mental health require robust and trustworthy research from across many disciplines. By spotlighting scientifically rigorous, adoptable solutions, this prize will help accelerate progress and provide a platform to those whose work has the potential to change people’s lives, to have an impact on policy and strengthen practice globally. I am delighted that we are able to partner with Wellcome on this award since showcasing multidisciplinary research that underpins progress lies at the very core of what we do at Nature and in the Nature Portfolio more broadly." The prize is now open for applications from research teams and small and medium-sized organisations worldwide with an application deadline of 18 September 2026. Submissions must demonstrate strong scientific rigour, be informed by lived experience and show clear potential to improve outcomes and transform lives at scale. Finalists will be announced in May 2027 and the winner announced in June 2027. The overall winner will receive USD 1 million, with three finalist teams awarded USD 250,000 each, alongside global recognition, enhanced visibility of their research and practical support via a development programme that helps progress their interventions towards adoption and policy integration. Backed by Wellcome and Nature , the prize brings together two global organisations renowned for their scientific excellence and investment in the international community. Wellcome is one of the world's leading funders of mental health research. The global health foundation supports new ways to intervene early in anxiety, depression and psychosis. The Nature Awards team will support the design and delivery of a globally visible, inclusive and credible prize. Entries will be assessed by an expert panel - which includes Magdalena Skipper, Editor-in-Chief of Nature, Professor Chyrell Bellamy, Yale School of Medicine and Obi Felten, Google X, Moonshot & Flourish Labs among many others - against four core criteria: novelty, credibility, effectiveness and adoptability alongside the strength of lived experience engagement. Celebrating these scientific breakthroughs will help accelerate the adoption of solutions that improve access to better treatments, interventions and care. Applications are open, with eligible research teams and small and medium-sized enterprises invited to apply here.
